rawFindings.title: Removed caching of base routes can cause incorrect behavior when defining multiple routes for the same path and method
rawFindings.explanation: The patch removes the entire _baseRoute method and changes all route retrievals to directly use this._router.route(path). Previously, _baseRoute tried to cache and reuse Route instances for the same path, preventing duplicate conflicting routes. Removing this cache leads to creating new Route objects on every call, which breaks the ability to override or accumulate route handlers for the same path reliably.
rawFindings.suggestion: Restore the _baseRoute method caching logic to ensure route uniqueness per path and consistent chaining of handlers. Change the methods.forEach and app.all implementations to use _baseRoute(path) instead of this._router.route(path). This reinstates the caching and fixes route handling for multiple app.VERB calls to the same path.

rawFindings.title: Potential removal of deprecated caching for base routes may affect existing apps
rawFindings.explanation: The patch removes the _baseRoutes cache and changes app.VERB and app.all methods to call this._router.route(path) directly instead of using _baseRoute(path) which cached routes. Removing caching may affect performance and behavior when multiple identical routes are added.
rawFindings.suggestion: If caching is required for functionality or performance, restore caching behavior or ensure this change is intentional and documented.

rawFindings.title: Incorrect use of internal method _baseRoute removed without replacement
rawFindings.explanation: The code removes usage of the internal `_baseRoute` method and directly calls `this._router.route(path)`. The `_baseRoute` method had internal logic to cache routes, improving efficiency and potentially avoiding duplicate route handling.
rawFindings.suggestion: Replace all calls to `this._router.route(path)` in app.VERB and app.all methods with the preserved `_baseRoute(path)` method or re-implement similar caching to ensure correct route reuse and prevent performance degradation or redefinition bugs.
